column1: # The checks of shell/boot-manager.nsh, the first UEFI Shell boot of boot-manager: the firmware's
# boot manager loaded it through Boot009A, which BootNext named and Linux created in boot 1, from
# the device path that get shows, and BootNext is gone; get shows Boot0099 and Key0099 as
# tests/qemu/vars/boot-manager.json seeds them, as Linux showed them; set-attributes refuses
# PlatformRecovery####, OsRecovery####, an absent load option and a flag both to set and to clear,
# create-load-option refuses Boot0099, which exists, and set-device-path ConOutDev, leaving the
# global variables as they were; set-attributes clears and sets Boot0099's LOAD_OPTION_ACTIVE,
# keeping its undefined bit, and Key0099 and Key009A follow it, and sets and clears
# Driver0000's LOAD_OPTION_FORCE_RECONNECT, as Linux did; create-load-option creates Boot009B, of
# the short-form File Path of uefisettings.efi, which BootNext then names; create-key refuses
# Key0099, which exists, and ALT-F11, the keys of Key009A that Linux created, and creates
# Key009B, SHIFT-F12 to Boot009B. See check-shell-log.sh.

column3: .value as $v | . == {"variable": "Boot009A-8be4df61-93ca-11d2-aa0d-00e098032b8c", "attributes": 7, "value": {"attributes": ["active"], "category": "boot", "description": "uefisettings Shell", "device_paths": $v.device_paths, "optional_data": ""}} and ($firmware | any(. == "BdsDxe: loading Boot009A \"\($v.description)\" from \($v.device_paths[0])"))
